thread:
Ava Chen: incident-bot alerted p99 streaming tail latency spike in eu-west2 at ~08:02 UTC. downstream streaming connections showing increased TLS handshake times and retries. paging SRE oncall. customer-impact: some live sessions experiencing stalls and reconnects.

monitoring-bot: ALERT p99_streaming_latency_eu-west2 > 1200ms, streaming_reconnect_rate x3 baseline, tls_handshake_95pct > 800ms.

Noelle (oncall-sre): on it. starting basic triage - checking routing, NAT, DNS. tagging netops. can folks avoid mass restarts until we know cause? :eyes:

Tom Rivera: noted, pulling netflow and proxy logs. early q: is this across zones or single AZ?

Ava Chen: initial heatmap shows cross-AZ spikes, particularly AZ-b -> AZ-c. path rtt to our egress NATs is fine, but TLS handshake tail is high.

Noelle (oncall-sre): running quick checks: 
```
# from eu-west2-proxy-03
ss -tn src :443 state established sport = :443 | grep -i tls
curl -v --resolve api.redwood-eu:443:10.21.9.8 https://api.redwood-eu/health
```

Tom Rivera: digging into iptables conntrack counts, seeing SNAT port churn on nat-01-eu. ephemeral port usage spiking near threshold on some hosts. output snippet: 
```
conntrack: entries=123456 used=98%
/proc/sys/net/ipv4/ip_local_port_range = 32768 60999
```

NetOps: we are seeing asymmetric pathing for some instances in AZ-b -> egress-nat pool 4. suspected route flaps at the cloud provider's internal router. raising a ticket with provider as well.

Maya Patel: customer impact estimate - two top paying customers have ~2% of sessions hitting stalls; overall request success still > 99% but streaming latency p99 > 2s for affected flows. CS notified.

Raj Singh (CS): looped in support; proactive outreach prepared if impact grows. collecting customer session ids.

Noelle (oncall-sre): mitigation plan: 1) divert new streaming sessions away from nat pool 4 via service mesh weights, 2) enable TLS keepalive tuning fallback, 3) enable short-term client-side reconnect smoothing. executing 1 now.

deploy-bot: mesh-route update applied: streaming-route weight nat-pool-4 -> 0.2, nat-pool-1/2 -> 0.8.

Tom Rivera: after divert, observed p95 improved ~300ms lower, p99 also trending down but still noisy. continuing deeper network traces.

NetOps: provider confirms internal routing noise affecting several host groups; they are rotating spine fabric and suspect control-plane reconvergence. mitigation options: move affected hosts to alternate egress or bump ephemeral port ranges.

Noelle (oncall-sre): bump ephemeral_ports and drain the most affected nodes. running runbook steps.

Ava Chen: running live verify on streaming tail metrics, toggling canary fallback for long-running streams to use short-id caching (reduces per-connection state). small change rolled.

Noelle (oncall-sre): handoff to NetOps for provider escalation and long-term fix, handing active incident to Tom for post-mitigation monitoring. I'll follow up with timeline and incident severity. paging the oncall rotation for continuity in 45m.

Tom Rivera: capturing packet captures for one affected flow, here are notes: SYN->FIN gap correlates with NAT ephemeral exhaustion retries; also observed repeated TLS SYN retransmits before full handshake. saved pcap to s3://redwood-incidents/5201234567/pcap1.pcap

NetOps: provider applied an internal reroute and we see decreased retransmit rates. they claim fix in progress. monitoring shows NAT port utilization returning to normal on drained hosts.

monitoring-bot: p99_streaming_latency_eu-west2 decreased from 2200ms -> 760ms over 12 minutes after diversion. reconnect rate down to baseline x1.1.

Maya Patel: CS update: notified affected customers and offered warm handoff if they report ongoing problems.

Noelle (oncall-sre): rolling summary for post-incident: probable root cause = provider routing/convergence causing asymmetric egress through a saturated nat-pool leading to ephemeral port pressure + increased TLS handshake tail/retransmits; mitigation = service mesh weight diversion, ephemeral port range bump, draining bad hosts, provider reroute. impact = transient p99 spikes and streaming stalls for a subset of sessions. severity set to P2.

Ava Chen: saving timeline, logs and runbook steps. will open incident report and assign follow-ups: 1) add ephemeral port monitoring alert earlier, 2) automation to failover streaming-route off unhealthy nat-pools, 3) run provider post-mortem.

Raj Singh (CS): tagging customers notified and handing off to customer success for any follow-up.

Noelle (oncall-sre): handing off to oncall rotation: @Noelle stepping down in 45m, @next-oncall will take final verification and postmortem notes. please escalate to SRE lead if p95 stays above 1s for >30m.

Tom Rivera: I'll keep a watch window for 2 hours and validate packet-level metrics.

NetOps: leaving provider ticket open, will request root cause timeline and whether they changed route dampening.

monitoring-bot: closing active incident page at 09:04 UTC (status: mitigated).

Ava Chen: quick retrospective notes to add to incident doc: test runbook path for mesh diversion, add runbook step to pre-warm alternate NAT pools, consider preemptive ephemeral port expansion automation for egress-heavy AZs.

Noelle (oncall-sre): thanks team. Will file action items and assign owners. :thumbsup:
